hints.title: Scattered Match Alignment Obstacle
hints.text: Two strings can match characters at scattered indices. When characters match, you want to extend the best prior match, and when they differ, you must choose the better subsequence excluding one character. How can you structure subproblem transitions without repeating evaluations?

hints.title: Character Match Diagonal Invariant
hints.text: If characters match, the longest common subsequence extends the diagonal subproblem by one; otherwise, it is the maximum of excluding the character from either string.

hints.title: 2D Tabulation Alignment Procedure
hints.text: Create a 2D table of size (m+1) x (n+1) initialized to 0. Iterate through each character of text1 with index i and text2 with index j. If characters match, set table[i][j] to 1 + table[i-1][j-1]. If they differ, set it to the maximum of table[i-1][j] and table[i][j-1]. Return table[m][n].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Fills an (M+1) x (N+1) DP matrix with constant time transitions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 2^M subsequences of text1 to test in text2 requires exponential time, failing for strings longer than 25 characters.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: 2D matrix tracks subproblem alignments in O(M*N) time and space (or O(min(M, N)) with rolling rows).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Setting up (M+1) x (N+1) table with 0-indexed string offsets, identifying diagonal match vs adjacent max mismatch.
